title: Continuous background automation for Papyrus sites
description:
Papyrus sites increasingly run work by themselves, unattended: the weekly knowledge run (PPY-dca7cd), reader snapshots, and next the trend-story pipeline (PPY-fb4dfa) and AI drafting. Today there are four separate execution paths (the CLI fetching cloud source and running tactus locally; amplify/functions/assignment-action dispatching seeded kinds by key; the papyrus-procedure-runner Lambda; the Fargate scheduled-job construct from PPY-dca7cd), repo .tac files drift from backend versions, monitors are the only trigger, the Lambda stops at 15 minutes, and local-pod sites cannot run packaged procedures. Direction approved by Ryan 2026-10-23.

Target design:
1. Git is the source of truth for procedure code. Core procedures ship in the wheel. Site procedures live in the site repo and are registered automatically on deploy. The console views and runs procedures; code changes go through PRs.
2. Automation records in each site's backend: trigger + procedure key + input template. Trigger kinds: monitor (exists), schedule, event (reference ingested, story approved, proposal enters review), manual (console Run button). Each record has enable/disable, a budget/timeout, a concurrency limit, an idempotency key and alarms.
3. One run contract (load the published version, record the run, execute, write back) with three runtimes: the runner Lambda (default); Fargate for procedures marked long or heavy (the knowledge pipeline becomes such an automation); a local pod with a local run ledger and a file lock. assignment-action's fixed key dispatch is retired.
4. Guardrails in the contract: a cost estimate per run; the projection lease for anything touching pages, and never reconcile; outputs go to review queues or Proposals, not straight to publish, unless a site opts in.
5. Console Automation page: schedules and triggers, recent runs with their LLM context, failures, enable/disable. It builds on the existing Administration -> Procedures panel.

Test site: Distinctive Mark. The first slices of this epic are built and tried on Distinctive's TTAB flow.

Acceptance criteria for the epic:
- Every child story/chore is closed with its acceptance criteria met.
- Any core or site procedure can run on a schedule, on an event, or manually on a cloud or local-pod site, through the one run contract.
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete) required for every behaviour change.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Scope includes sites with no cloud backend: Papyrus sites that run from a local pod (for example Tactus-web) get the same background jobs through a local-pod runner (PPY-93faf2). Both runners share one job definition (PPY-433383). Order: packaging (PPY-e95a0c) → kind headers (PPY-0d4984) → desk cleanup (PPY-54bd13) → job definition (PPY-433383) → local-pod runner (PPY-93faf2) and site procedures (PPY-1b2edd).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Build order (supersedes the earlier order comments). Priorities are all 1 so none decreases along the order.
1. PPY-e95a0c  Ship Tactus procedures in the wheel (S)
2. PPY-0d4984  Kind headers validated against the registry (S)
3. PPY-54bd13  Remove desk vocabulary (S)
4. PPY-1b2edd  Register site and core procedures automatically on deploy (S)
5. PPY-433383  One procedure run contract across Lambda, Fargate and local-pod runtimes (L)
6. Automation records: triggers bound to procedures (M)
7. Automation outputs go to review by default (S)
8. Console Automation page (M)
9. PPY-93faf2  Run background jobs on a local pod, with no cloud backend (M)
10. PPY-ab6a50  Human review points: flags, timed soft reviews and hard approval gates (M)
11. PPY-1cd261  CMS console Notification Center (M)
12. PPY-f09147  Story-state triggers: bots act as a story moves between states (M)
13. PPY-b3aaea  Story similarity index and group locks (M)
14. PPY-8ffc18  Idea pipeline: research digest, weekly trends, idea synthesis into Proposals (L); subsumes PPY-fb4dfa
15. PPY-c4f8b8  Cross-story editorial checks with merge, split and series operations (L)
Note: the human review points story is a dependency of the story-state triggers, similarity index and idea pipeline stories, so in practice it can start as soon as the run contract and automation records exist; the Notification Center is its console UI. Priorities are all 1.

comments.text:
Status 2026-10-23 (end of day, before a usage pause).
Done and merged to develop: PPY-2e6e2b automation records (#630, released 5.32.0); PPY-112007 slice 2: enabled, limits, cost, run now (#639); review requests and the Notification Center as the console home v0 (#642); idea pipeline v0 (#641) wired to review requests (#651); the PPY-36ee96 docs task filed.
Release: promotion PR #649 to 5.33.0 is in CI and merges by itself when green; #650 and #651 follow in the next release.
Distinctive (test site): TTAB automation record created (slice 1 tested). The slice 2 router deploy waits for the release plus Distinctive's OK, after the Cyclotron router change sets.
Open decisions for Ryan: Data Parade articles' consent (reuse CookieYes vs the Papyrus banner); Shipped's switch to standard consent (confirm directly in the Shipped thread); auto-accept policy for Cyclotron-delivered pending references (proposed: a soft review per batch).
Blocked: the Cyclotron criteria migration (p.apyr.us fix, plus the Data Parade and Pilobolus classifiers): the lab's Anthus workspace returns 'API call failed', and the Cyclotron session is diagnosing.
